pattern_name: Relative clauses (who / which / that / where / whose)
pattern_name_ar: جُمل الوصل (who / which / that / where / whose)
formula: noun + who (people) / which (things) / that (both) / where (places) / whose (possession) + clause
formula_visual: [the man] + [who lives next door] + [is a doctor]
when_to_use: To add information about a noun inside one sentence instead of two: who for people, which for things, that for either (informal), where for places, whose for possession. Defining clauses take no commas; extra-information clauses take commas and cannot use 'that'.
when_to_use_ar: لإضافة معلومة عن اسم داخل جملة واحدة بدل جملتين: who للأشخاص، which للأشياء، that للاثنين، where للأماكن، whose للملكية. الجملة المحدِّدة بدون فواصل، والإضافية بفواصل ولا تستخدم that.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic relative clauses repeat the object as a pronoun (الرجل الذي رأيته), so learners say 'the man who I saw him'. They also use 'which' for people and 'who' for things, and add commas to defining clauses.

examples.en: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
This is the book which changed my life.
That's the café where we first met.
examples.ar: هذا المقهى الذي تقابلنا فيه أول مرة

examples.en: She's the student whose project won.
My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting us.
examples.ar: أخي، الذي يسكن في دبي، سيزورنا

common_errors.wrong: The man who I saw him was tall.
common_errors.correct: The man who I saw was tall.
common_errors.explanation: Don't repeat the object pronoun after the relative pronoun.

common_errors.wrong: The book who I read was great.
common_errors.correct: The book which/that I read was great.
common_errors.explanation: 'who' is for people; things take which/that.

common_errors.wrong: My brother, that lives in Dubai, is visiting.
common_errors.correct: My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting.
common_errors.explanation: 'that' cannot be used in extra-information clauses with commas.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: The woman ___ helped me was very kind.
This is the phone ___ I bought yesterday.
That's the hotel ___ we stayed last year.
He's the man ___ car was stolen.
My teacher, ___ is from Canada, speaks Arabic too.

quick_rule: People → who · things → which · either → that · places → where · possession → whose. Never repeat the object pronoun.
quick_rule_ar: أشخاص → who · أشياء → which · الاثنان → that · أماكن → where · ملكية → whose. لا تُعِد ضمير المفعول.
mnemonic: One noun, one relative pronoun, no extra 'him/it'.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 10 you practised weak who/that inside the flow. Say: 'the MAN whu lives next DOOR' — the relative pronoun is light and unstressed, gluing the two ideas together.
